setting.name: Strip mall, east Orlando
setting.desc: A burger counter in a tired strip mall off a six-lane road in east Orlando, between a vape shop and a tax preparer. Few people walk in; the parking lot is full of delivery drivers waiting for bags, and the tablets on the counter never stop chiming.

ev.text: A hurricane watch shut the region for two days. The apps went quiet, then flooded with orders the day after.
Drivers are double-parking and blocking the vape shop; the landlord sent a letter about the parking lot.

desk.title: The licensor's quality audit
desk.text: A mystery-shopper report says two MrBeast Burger orders arrived with cold fries and one with an undercooked patty.

log.text: December 2020. A year ago this was a franchise burger unit that was losing money every week; you de-branded it, kept the grill and the fryers, and scraped through the spring on takeout. Last month you signed with Virtual Dining Concepts: from tonight your kitchen also cooks MrBeast Burger and Mariah's Cookies for the delivery apps. VDC handles the brand and the marketing and takes a cut of every order; the apps take theirs. The launch is going to be enormous. Nobody knows how long it lasts.

world.notes: MrBeast Burger was launched by Virtual Dining Concepts (Orlando) under a September 2020 endorsement agreement and went live in December 2020, cooked by existing restaurants for delivery and pickup only. It sold more than a million burgers in its first three months and reached about 1,700 locations worldwide by the end of 2022. In 2023 MrBeast sued VDC to end the deal over undercooked, cold and 'inedible' food, saying more than half the locations averaged under two stars and he hadn't received a dime; VDC countersued for more than $100 million. Operators paid VDC 35-40% of sales, which covered brand and delivery relations, leaving about 30% after food and packaging (Nation's Restaurant News); one VDC operator paid DoorDash 30% on its virtual orders and VDC covered the marketing (Food On Demand). DoorDash's merchant plans charge 15%, 25% or 30%. Ghost-kitchen units rent for about $2,500-5,500 a month with hood and utilities. The restaurant, its staff, the suppliers, rent and local events are invented; the licensing fee is an estimate within the reported range, and order volumes are modelled, not reported figures.
